WITH pl AS (
  SELECT p.hostlink AS hostlink, s.hostplname AS hostplname, o.period AS period,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.hostlink ORDER BY o.period ASC) AS rn
  FROM planets p
  JOIN orbital_characteristics o ON o.bodylink = p.planetref
  JOIN stars s ON s.stellarref = p.hostlink
  WHERE o.period IS NOT NULL AND o.period > 0 AND s.compcount > 1
),
pairs AS (
  SELECT a.hostlink AS hostlink, a.hostplname AS hostplname, b.period / a.period AS ratio
  FROM pl a
  JOIN pl b ON b.hostlink = a.hostlink AND b.rn = a.rn + 1
)
SELECT pairs.hostplname AS host_star_name,
       ROUND(EXP(AVG(LN(pairs.ratio))), 3) AS geometric_mean_period_ratio
FROM pairs
GROUP BY pairs.hostlink, pairs.hostplname
HAVING MAX(pairs.ratio) < 3
   AND (SELECT pl.period FROM pl WHERE pl.hostlink = pairs.hostlink AND pl.rn = 1) < 10
ORDER BY geometric_mean_period_ratio DESC;
note: Compact system = multi-planet star (stars.compcount > 1) where every adjacent period ratio < 3; adjacency and 'innermost' are taken on orbital period order. Only planets with a known positive period contribute, so systems with missing periods are judged on the periods that exist. 210 systems returned.

WITH cand AS (
  SELECT pp.massjup * 317.83 AS mass_earth,
         pp.radjup * 11.209 AS radius_earth
  FROM physical_properties pp
  WHERE pp.massjup IS NOT NULL AND pp.massjup <> 0
    AND pp.radjup IS NOT NULL AND pp.radjup <> 0
)
SELECT ROUND(SQRT(2 * 6.674E-11 * (cand.mass_earth * 5.972E24) / (cand.radius_earth * 6.371E6)) / 1000.0, 0) AS escape_velocity_km_s
FROM cand
ORDER BY cand.mass_earth / cand.radius_earth DESC
LIMIT 1;
note: Highest mass-radius ratio is Kepler-57 b (MRR 2742); escape velocity 585.8 -> 586 km/s. Earth mass 5.972e24 kg, Earth radius 6.371e6 m and G = 6.674e-11 are assumed (the knowledge file does not give them); using G = 6.67430e-11 still rounds to 586.

SELECT CASE
         WHEN LOWER(TRIM(json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.photometry.Photo_Band'))) IN ('v (johnson)','johnson','v','johnson v','v-band') THEN 'v-band'
         WHEN LOWER(TRIM(json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.photometry.Photo_Band'))) IN ('kepler-band','kepler','kep-b','kep') THEN 'kepler-band'
       END AS photometric_band,
       COUNT(*) AS star_count
FROM stars s
WHERE json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.photometry.Photo_Band') IS NOT NULL
  AND LOWER(TRIM(json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.photometry.Photo_Band'))) IN
      ('v (johnson)','johnson','v','johnson v','v-band','kepler-band','kepler','kep-b','kep')
GROUP BY photometric_band
ORDER BY star_count DESC;
note: Band lives in stars.stellarprops -> photometry.Photo_Band. The raw values are exactly the nine listed labels plus 'k-band' (315, ignored) and NULL (109). Result: kepler-band 1306, v-band 779.

WITH st AS (
  SELECT s.stellarref AS stellarref,
         json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.physical.Radius_Value') AS r_star,
         json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.physical.Temp_Value') AS t_star
  FROM stars s
),
pl AS (
  SELECT p.hostlink AS hostlink, pp.massjup AS massjup, pp.densvalue AS densvalue
  FROM planets p
  JOIN physical_properties pp ON pp.objectlink = p.planetref
  WHERE pp.densvalue IS NOT NULL OR pp.massjup IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG((st.r_star * st.r_star) * POWER(st.t_star / 5778.0, 4)), 4) AS avg_stellar_luminosity
FROM st
WHERE st.r_star IS NOT NULL AND st.t_star IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pl WHERE pl.hostlink = st.stellarref AND pl.densvalue > 3)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pl WHERE pl.hostlink = st.stellarref AND pl.massjup > 0.1);
note: Rocky = density > 3 g/cm3, gas giant = mass > 0.1 MJ, both drawn from the same planet pool restricted to rows with a known density or mass. 27 stars qualify; result 0.9621.

answer:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS planet_count
FROM physical_properties pp
JOIN data_quality_tracking dq ON dq.targetlink = pp.objectlink
WHERE pp.radjup IS NOT NULL
  AND json_extract(dq.limitflags, '$.planetary_limits.Rad_Lim') = 1;
note: Rad_Lim in data_quality_tracking.limitflags is the upper-limit flag: 2693 rows are 0, 678 NULL and exactly 1 is 1, so the answer is 1. The low count is surprising but the flag distribution leaves no alternative reading.

WITH mp AS (
  SELECT s.stellarref AS stellarref, s.hostplname AS hostplname,
         json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.physical.Mass_Value') AS recorded_mass
  FROM stars s
  WHERE s.compcount > 1
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT p.hostlink AS hostlink, o.semimajor AS semimajor, o.period AS period,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.hostlink ORDER BY o.semimajor DESC) AS rn
  FROM planets p
  JOIN orbital_characteristics o ON o.bodylink = p.planetref
  WHERE o.semimajor IS NOT NULL AND o.period IS NOT NULL AND o.period > 0
)
SELECT mp.hostplname AS host_star_name,
       mp.recorded_mass AS recorded_stellar_mass,
       (r.semimajor * r.semimajor * r.semimajor) / ((r.period / 365.25) * (r.period / 365.25)) AS calculated_stellar_mass
FROM mp
JOIN ranked r ON r.hostlink = mp.stellarref AND r.rn = 1
ORDER BY ABS(mp.recorded_mass - (r.semimajor * r.semimajor * r.semimajor) / ((r.period / 365.25) * (r.period / 365.25))) ASC;
note: Period converted days->years with 365.25; calculated masses reproduce the recorded ones to ~4 decimals, which confirms the unit handling. The question states only the 'known and positive period' filter, so stars whose recorded mass is NULL are kept (115 of 465 rows) and sort first under ASC; if the intent was to compare only known masses, add 'AND mp.recorded_mass IS NOT NULL'.

SELECT s.hostplname || ' ' || p.completter AS planet_full_name,
       s.hostplname AS host_star_name,
       o.eccentricity AS eccentricity,
       ROUND((pp.massjup * 1.898E27) / (json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.physical.Mass_Value') * 1.98847E30), 5) AS planet_star_mass_ratio
FROM planets p
JOIN stars s ON s.stellarref = p.hostlink
JOIN physical_properties pp ON pp.objectlink = p.planetref
JOIN orbital_characteristics o ON o.bodylink = p.planetref
JOIN data_quality_tracking d ON d.targetlink = p.planetref
WHERE o.eccentricity > 0.25
  AND LOWER(d.masssource) = 'msini'
  AND pp.massjup IS NOT NULL
  AND json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.physical.Mass_Value') IS NOT NULL
  AND json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.physical.Mass_Value') > 0
ORDER BY planet_star_mass_ratio ASC;
note: Minimum-mass flag read from data_quality_tracking.masssource; LOWER(masssource) = 'msini' matches 554 rows (the 9 'Msin(i)/sin(i)' rows are excluded as they are not the literal 'msini'). Planet full name built as host star name + component letter, since planets holds only the letter. 177 rows; at 5 dp most ratios collapse to a handful of distinct values.

WITH cand AS (
  SELECT pp.massjup AS massjup,
         pp.massjup * 317.83 AS mass_earth,
         pp.radjup * 11.209 AS radius_earth,
         json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.physical.Mass_Value') AS star_mass
  FROM physical_properties pp
  JOIN planets p ON p.planetref = pp.objectlink
  JOIN stars s ON s.stellarref = p.hostlink
  WHERE pp.massjup IS NOT NULL AND pp.radjup IS NOT NULL AND pp.densvalue IS NOT NULL
    AND pp.densvalue > 3
    AND pp.massjup * 317.83 BETWEEN 1 AND 10
    AND json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.physical.Mass_Value') IS NOT NULL
    AND json_extract(s.stellarprops, '$.physical.Mass_Value') > 0
)
SELECT printf('%.6e', (cand.massjup * 1.898E27) / (cand.star_mass * 1.98847E30)) AS planet_star_mass_ratio
FROM cand
ORDER BY cand.mass_earth / (cand.radius_earth * cand.radius_earth) DESC
LIMIT 1;
note: Winner is Kepler-131 c (g = 11.69 Earth g); ratio 2.433046e-05. Jupiter/Sun mass constants taken from the sibling question since this one does not restate them. '7 digits of precision' read as 7 significant figures, i.e. printf('%.6e').
